On Sat, Apr 18, 2026 at 8:12 AM Maya <support@redwood.ai> wrote:
> We started seeing a sharp increase in 429 and 5xx responses across several customer routes at ~08:05 PT...

We are seeing correlated Route53 latency spikes and elevated "no route" NXDOMAIN counts from our DNS vendor (dnsco.io). CloudWatch shows upstream API throttling errors from a small subset of EC2 worker pools serving the Dedicated clusters. Initial hypothesis: intermittent DNS resolution failures are cascading into retry storms at our edge, causing connection timeouts and upstream 5xx when connections finally exhaust.

Immediate mitigations enacted (08:18):
- Disabled aggressive client-side retries for affected routes (reduced retry multiplier in edge config).
- Enabled soft-fail fast path that returns 503 with controlled backoff for a short window.
- Scale-up: spun additional workers in eu-west-1 and us-west-2 (temporary) to absorb load while we investigate.

Next steps: open AWS support case, contact dnsco support, and prepare an exec summary for Sales/CS to send to impacted customers. Marcus, can you validate if Dedicated pools for FinTechCo were pinned to a single AZ?

Rishi
VP, Platform Reliability

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-04-18T08:34:02-07:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] Production 429/5xx spike — multiple customers reporting timeouts

Confirmed — FinTechCo's Dedicated pool was pinned to a two-AZ configuration but had a narrow spread of instances in us-west-2. When the DNS flakiness pushed traffic unevenly, the pool exhausted ephemeral connections and our edge layer started returning 5xx. We're seeing a pattern where upstream DNS timeouts (~200-600ms) push many parallel connection attempts which then hit socket limits.

I recommend the following to stabilize customers immediately:
1) Apply temporary connection queueing at the edge (limit concurrent upstream connects per client IP).
2) Push a config change to reduce retry attempts from 3 -> 1 for 2 minutes for high-volume routes.
3) Increase socket/connection limits on worker hosts as an emergency measure.
4) Ask Sales/CS to send a short message to customers acknowledging we are actively mitigating and we expect improvements in the next 30-45 minutes.

I'll implement (1) and (3) now and coordinate with infra for a faster scale.

Marcus
Director, Serving Runtime

Subject: Exec brief: FinTechCo & Acme incident — summary and asks

Executive summary (for CRO/CEO) — 11:03 PT
- Impact: Between 08:05–09:30 PT we observed a surge in 429 and 5xx responses affecting ~12% of total requests for a 40-minute window; highest impact for two Dedicated customers (FinTechCo, Acme Payments). No data loss, but higher latency and request failures caused customer-facing errors.
- Root cause (prelim): Intermittent DNS resolution failures from our DNS provider (dnsco.io) increased upstream latencies and triggered retry storms at the edge. This exposed connection limits and resulted in worker-side 5xx.
- Mitigations taken: reduced retries, enforced per-client concurrent connect caps, scaled additional workers, and engaged AWS & DNS vendor support. Observed recovery: 5xx down to ~1.5% and 429 to ~3% by 10:55 PT.
- Business asks for execs:
  1) Approve up to $50k emergency support/credits if the two impacted customers request financial remediation (Customer Success will provide proposed credit amounts).
  2) Approve priority budget to accelerate multi-DNS fallback and longer-term hardened retry logic (estimate: 2 Sprints, ~6 FTE-weeks).
  3) Authorize an external postmortem communication to impacted customers within 48 hours.

I'm available to brief further. Marcus and Rishi are preparing a technical RCA and remediation plan; we'll share an internal timeline today.

Sean Gallagher
Head of Revenue Operations
